Based on the analysis results, annealing reduces the grain size and increases the grain boundary density in the Al15Ti35V20Nb15Zr15 alloy. The enhanced grain boundary strengthening effect hinders dislocation motion, thereby improving the alloy's strength, which is consistent with the Hall–Petch relationship.

Calculations and studies [ 33, 34 ] indicate that the second-phase strengthening contributes approximately σpre = 1060 MPa. As shown in Table 4, when second phases are present, their strengthening effect exceeds the contributions from other mechanisms. Thus, second-phase strengthening is the primary mechanism in this study.
